Law Passed: Alaska HB 25 (Disposable Food Service Ware) passed both chambers of the 34th Legislature with bipartisan support but was vetoed by Governor Mike Dunleavy on June 24–25, 2026. No veto override was pursued. No EPR packaging law of any kind is in effect in Alaska. The 34th Legislature has adjourned; any future bill must be reintroduced in the 35th Legislature (2027).
Status Detail: HB 25 would have banned single-use polystyrene foam foodware in restaurants and state agency operations starting January 1, 2027. It passed the House 25–15 and the Senate 13–7, but the combined vote of 38–22 fell short of the 40 needed for a veto override. Governor Dunleavy cited the bill's 2027 effective date as creating an unrealistic implementation timeline. No broader EPR packaging bill covering films, bags, or other packaging materials was introduced or advanced in Alaska during the 2025–2026 legislative session.

Law Passed: California SB 54 (Plastic Pollution Prevention and Packaging Producer Responsibility Act), enacted June 2022; permanent implementing regulations approved by the Office of Administrative Law on May 1, 2026 and now in effect. The program covers all single-use packaging (including plastic film, bags, flexible packaging, paper-based packaging, and food service ware) sold, distributed, or imported into California.
Status Detail: Permanent regulations took effect May 1, 2026, triggering immediate producer registration and reporting obligations. CAA submitted its draft California Program Plan to the SB 54 Advisory Board on June 15, 2026; a public comment period closed August 14, 2026, and CAA must submit the final Program Plan to CalRecycle by October 13, 2026 for approval by January 1, 2027, when full program enforcement begins. Two active lawsuits challenge the regulations — a June 2, 2026 state court suit by NRDC/Californians Against Waste over alleged regulatory loopholes, and a June 22, 2026 federal suit by a 17-state coalition and NAW raising constitutional objections — but neither has resulted in a stay or injunction, and compliance obligations remain in effect.

Law Passed: Connecticut has no enacted packaging EPR law. HB 6917 (2025), which called for a feasibility study on packaging EPR, passed the House 138-0 but died on the Senate calendar. In the 2026 session, HB 5151 — which would have required EPR-related recommendations based on Connecticut's waste characterization study — also died in committee. Connecticut SB 457, signed June 4, 2026, addresses the state's bottle bill (beverage container producer responsibility) and is a separate instrument from broad packaging EPR.
Status Detail: Connecticut has no packaging EPR law and no enacted packaging EPR study mandate as of September 2026. The 2025 substitute HB 6917 passed the House unanimously but died on the Senate calendar; the 2026 HB 5151 died in committee when the legislative session ended. Connecticut is characterized by industry observers as a state that could see a packaging EPR bill advance in 2027 or 2028 but has not done so yet.

Law Passed: Florida has no EPR packaging law passed or pending. The 2026 legislative session (January 13 – March 13, 2026) adjourned without introducing or advancing any EPR packaging bill. HB 6225 (stand-alone EPR bill from a prior session) stalled in committee and has not been reintroduced. The state actively opposes EPR-related industry coordination: Florida AG Uthmeier led a multistate coalition sending antitrust warning letters in October 2025 to the Sustainable Packaging Coalition and Consumer Goods Forum, and follow-up letters to nearly 80 corporations in February 2026.
Status Detail: Florida's 2026 regular legislative session ended March 13, 2026 with no EPR packaging bill introduced or advanced. The state also maintains preemption laws that prevent local governments from independently regulating most single-use plastics and packaging. Florida's Attorney General has taken an affirmatively hostile posture toward EPR-aligned industry groups, issuing antitrust civil investigative demands against the Sustainable Packaging Coalition and U.S. Plastics Pact and warning corporations against participation in those organizations.

Law Passed: HB 750 (Act 103, Session Laws of Hawaii 2025) signed into law May 27, 2025. Requires the Hawaii Department of Health to conduct a statewide packaging EPR needs assessment covering packaging materials (paper, paperboard, cardboard, plastics, glass, metal, and mixed materials) and paper products. A companion full EPR bill, HB 1264, was introduced in the 2025 session but did not advance beyond committee referral. The 2026 legislative session adjourned sine die without new packaging EPR legislation passing; four non-binding labeling study resolutions introduced in March 2026 also did not advance. The needs assessment advisory board held its first meeting in late summer 2026 and is actively assembling.
Status Detail: HB 750 (Act 103) is enacted law; the Hawaii Department of Health began needs assessment work in July 2025 and the advisory council had its first formal meeting in late August/early September 2026. The final needs assessment report is due to the legislature by December 31, 2027. No comprehensive EPR program legislation has been enacted; Hawaii remains in a pre-EPR study phase.

Law Passed: Illinois has no enacted packaging EPR law. Public Act 103-0383 (SB 1555, signed July 2023) established the Statewide Recycling Needs Assessment Advisory Council and directed Illinois EPA to conduct a packaging and paper products needs assessment, with final recommendations due to the General Assembly and Governor by December 1, 2026. Separately, HB 4064 (the Extended Producer Responsibility and Recycling Refund Act), introduced May 21, 2025, is pending in the House Rules Committee with no action since introduction. Senate companion SB 1817 contains only a short-title provision and no substantive text.
Status Detail: HB 4064 is stalled in the House Rules Committee, with legislative movement effectively gated on the Statewide Recycling Needs Assessment report due December 1, 2026. No producer obligations, fees, or PRO requirements are in effect in Illinois today. The needs assessment advisory council is actively meeting and is expected to deliver policy recommendations that could shape a full EPR bill in the 2027 session.

Law Passed: Maine's packaging EPR law (LD 1541, 38 M.R.S. §2146, enacted July 2021) was amended by LD 1423 (signed June 20, 2025). The program covers all consumer packaging material types regardless of substrate — plastic (including film/poly bags and flexible packaging), paper (including paper bags and paper-based packaging), glass, metal, and cardboard. Implementation is stalled: the Stewardship Organization RFP closed August 18, 2026 with zero proposals submitted, and on September 11, 2026 Maine DEP announced it will revise and reissue the RFP.
Status Detail: Maine DEP published its Stewardship Organization RFP on June 15, 2026, but received no proposals by the August 18, 2026 deadline; Circular Action Alliance — the sole expected bidder and the PRO in all six other EPR states — declined to bid, citing misalignment between the RFP scope and its operational model. On September 11, 2026, DEP announced it will revise the RFP and reissue it. With no Stewardship Organization under contract, producers currently have no active registration, reporting, or fee obligations, and all previously stated implementation dates (including late-2026 registration and invoicing) are no longer in effect.

Law Passed: Maryland SB 901 (Packaging and Paper Products – Producer Responsibility Plans Act) was signed into law on May 13, 2025, and its first implementing regulations (COMAR 26.04.14) became effective May 25, 2026. The law covers all packaging and paper products — including primary, secondary, and tertiary packaging materials such as plastic film/bags, paper bags, and mesh/bulk-good bags — sold, offered for sale, imported, or distributed in Maryland.
Status Detail: The program is now in its active registration and early-compliance phase: implementing regulations took effect May 25, 2026, and CAA (the only currently registered PRO) was required to submit its producer, brand, and material list to MDE by July 1, 2026. Fees are not yet active; the PRO five-year producer responsibility plan is due July 1, 2028, after which a cost-share ramp begins (50% of net recycling costs by 2028, 75% by 2029, 90% by 2030). MDE has indicated additional rulemakings will follow to address full reporting categories, fee structures, and other program details.

Law Passed: North Carolina HB 882 (Break Free From Plastic & Forever Chemicals Act, 2025-2026 session) — pending in the House Rules, Calendar, and Operations Committee; no passage.
Status Detail: HB 882 was introduced on April 9, 2025, and referred to the House Rules, Calendar, and Operations Committee on April 10, 2025, where it has stalled. The bill would establish a full EPR framework for all packaging materials (including plastic film, poly bags, paper, and other packaging types), require producers to join a Producer Responsibility Organization, mandate post-consumer content targets, ban PFAS and other toxic substances in packaging, and appropriate $100,000 to DEQ for implementation. As of the most recent tracking through mid-2026, no further committee action or floor vote has occurred, and the bill remains at 25% progression with no amendments or renumbering reported.

Law Passed: Oklahoma HB 4068 (2026), an environmental marketing claims/greenwashing bill covering product and packaging labels, was introduced in February 2026 but died in committee without a vote before the legislative session ended May 29, 2026. No EPR packaging law has been introduced or passed in Oklahoma.
Status Detail: Oklahoma HB 4068 would have prohibited use of recycling symbols or environmental benefit claims (recyclable, compostable, biodegradable, carbon neutral, eco-friendly, etc.) on products and packaging unless substantiated against defined criteria, with civil penalties up to $2,500. The bill remained in committee for at least three weeks with no formal votes called and did not advance before the 2026 session adjourned sine die. Oklahoma has no enacted or pending EPR packaging law requiring producer registration, fees, or a Producer Responsibility Organization.

Law Passed: Rhode Island H 6207 (EPR needs assessment) signed into law June 30, 2025. Full EPR packaging bills H 7910, S 2656, and H 7911 introduced February 27, 2026; H 7910 and H 7911 received a committee hearing on May 27, 2026 and were held for further study; S 2656 remains under committee review. No full EPR program has been enacted.
Status Detail: H 6207, signed by Gov. Dan McKee on June 30, 2025, mandates a third-party statewide recycling and waste-management gap analysis with the final needs assessment report due to the Governor by December 1, 2026 (draft due to RIDEM September 1, 2026). Three full packaging EPR bills — H 7910, S 2656, and H 7911 — were introduced in the 2026 session on February 27, 2026; H 7910 and H 7911 were heard by the House Environment and Natural Resources Committee on May 27, 2026 and recommended to be held for further study, while S 2656 remains under committee review. Rhode Island currently has no operative EPR program and no producer compliance obligations.

Law Passed: Tennessee SB 0269 / HB 600 (Tennessee Waste to Jobs Act) — packaging EPR bill introduced January 2025, amended in early 2026, sidelined in committee March 2026, and declared dead on April 24, 2026 at end of the 114th General Assembly session. No law enacted. Sponsor has committed to reintroduction in 2027.
Status Detail: SB 0269 / HB 600 failed to advance out of the Senate Energy, Agriculture and Natural Resources Committee on March 11, 2026, and the bill was formally marked dead on April 24, 2026 when the 114th General Assembly adjourned. The bill would have required producers of packaging materials — including all covered packaging formats — to join a Producer Responsibility Organization and fund recycling programs, with exemptions for businesses under $10M in annual revenue and counties under 200,000 residents. Sponsor Sen. Heidi Campbell has vowed to reintroduce in 2027; per SPC, Tennessee's bill will need to be fully reintroduced in the new session as it does not carry over.

Law Passed: Vermont S.139 (2025-2026 session), 'An act relating to the management of materials from packaging,' was introduced April 2, 2025 and died in the Senate Committee on Natural Resources and Energy without advancing. No packaging EPR law has passed, and no new packaging EPR bill is currently active in the Vermont legislature.
Status Detail: S.139 would have required a needs assessment on the management of packaging materials distributed in Vermont, covering opportunities to improve reuse, recyclability, safety, and reduction of packaging toxicity and quantity. The bill stalled in committee and did not advance. Vermont is viewed as a state that could reintroduce packaging EPR legislation in 2027 or 2028, but any future bill will need to be newly introduced.

Law Passed: Virginia has a packaging EPR bill pending that carried over from the 2026 legislative session to 2027; no packaging EPR law has been enacted.
Status Detail: Virginia's 2026 General Assembly session concluded in mid-March 2026 without passing packaging EPR legislation. The bill is one of only two states (alongside New Jersey) whose packaging EPR bill carries over to the 2027 session rather than requiring full reintroduction. Holland & Knight (January 2026) identified Virginia as a state with a pending proposal from a prior legislative session. Virginia's governor also vetoed HB 86, a mattress stewardship EPR bill, in April 2026, signaling executive skepticism toward EPR-style fee mandates in the current political environment.

Law Passed: Washington E2SSB 5284 (Recycling Reform Act) signed into law May 17, 2025; effective July 27, 2025. The law establishes an EPR program covering glass, plastic (including wraps, films, and bags), paper, and metal packaging and paper products sold to residential consumers. The Washington Department of Ecology is now in active Phase 1 implementation: rulemaking underway (Chapter 173-950 WAC), a preliminary statewide collection list was open for public comment August 5–19, 2026, and finalized collection lists are due by October 2026.
Status Detail: The law (codified as Chapter 70A.208 RCW) requires producers of covered packaging and paper products to join or form a Producer Responsibility Organization (PRO) by July 1, 2026, with the PRO required to have registered with Ecology by March 1, 2026. Circular Action Alliance (CAA) registered as the PRO on behalf of producers. Ecology is conducting rulemaking and published preliminary statewide collection lists for public comment in August 2026; final lists are due by October 1, 2026. Full program implementation, including curbside recycling cost reimbursements to service providers, begins January 1, 2030.

Law Passed: Wisconsin AB 772 and companion SB 778 — packaging EPR bills introduced in December 2025 — failed to pass before the March 2026 legislative session deadline and are now dead for this session; reintroduction expected in 2027.
Status Detail: Companion bills AB 772 (Assembly) and SB 778 (Senate) were introduced in December 2025 and referred to their respective committees, but neither advanced before the Wisconsin legislature's March 2026 session deadline. Both bills are now effectively expired for the 2025-2026 session and would need to be reintroduced in a future session to move forward. The primary Assembly sponsor, Rep. Snodgrass, has publicly acknowledged the bills will not pass this session but intends to reintroduce them.
